mainTopic: When found corpses form a שכונת קברות, and what תפוסה (the earth taken with a corpse) is and how much of it is taken.
overview: The משנה finishes its rule about finding three corpses. Since it may be an old burial area, you check twenty אמות outward, and you may no longer simply move the bodies away. The גמרא then reads the משנה closely. רב יהודה says a known grave, a killed person, someone buried sitting, or someone buried with his head between his thighs does not count. עולא בר חנינא teaches a ברייתא that a corpse missing a part has no תפוסה and no שכונת קברות. The unusual burials are explained by one idea: maybe the dead person was a גוי. The ברייתא adds that bodies lying head-to-feet do not count. Known graves and newly found bodies do not join together, as רבי עקיבא told רבי ישבב. The גמרא then learns תפוסה from יעקב's words 'carry me out of Egypt.' It settles an apparent contradiction about how much earth to take: the three-fingerbreadths measure is בן עזאי's view. Finally it turns to the משנה's next words about checking from the spot.

steps.title: Checking twenty cubits around a possible burial area
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends its rule: after finding three corpses, you search twenty אמות outward. If you find another one, you search twenty more. A single corpse could have been moved away with its surrounding earth, but a burial area cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: He checks from that spot outward for twenty cubits. If he finds one more at the end of the twenty cubits, he checks another twenty cubits outward from there, because there is good reason to expect more. If he had found the body alone at first, he could have taken it away together with the earth around it.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה is finishing its rule about someone who finds three corpses lying in the normal burial way. It tells him to keep searching outward, because this may be an old burial area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Three bodies suggest a forgotten graveyard, so we expect more graves nearby. That is why each new find means checking another twenty אמות. A single body is different: you may remove it with its תפוסה, the earth around it. Once the place is treated as a burial area, that option is gone.

keyTerms.meaning: He checks or searches
A cubit, a measure of about an arm's length
There is good reason to suspect it
The earth around a corpse that must be removed together with it

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the practical result of the whole משנה. A burial area changes what you are allowed to do with the bodies and how far you must search.

phrases.english: He checks from it and onward twenty cubits,
phrases.notes: "From it" means from the spot where the three bodies were found.

phrases.english: if he found one at the end of twenty cubits —
he checks from it and onward twenty cubits.
For there is a basis for the matter.
For had he found it at first,
phrases.notes: "At first" means found by itself, before it was part of a group of three.

phrases.english: he would take it and its surrounding earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's rule about finding three corpses.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: After finding three corpses, one searches twenty אמות outward, and again after each new find. The bodies may not be moved with their תפוסה as a single body could be.

steps.title: רב יהודה reads exclusions from each word of the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה learns four limits from the words of the משנה: מצא, מת, מושכב and כדרכו. Each word leaves out a certain kind of corpse from forming a burial area.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: "Found" leaves out a body that was already known. "Dead" leaves out a person who was killed. "Lying" leaves out one who is sitting. "In his normal way" leaves out one whose head was placed between his thighs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. רב יהודה goes through the משנה's words one by one and shows what each word leaves out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word narrows the case. The משנה speaks of bodies found now for the first time, so a grave that was already known does not join with them. A killed person may have been buried right where he fell. Someone buried sitting, or bent over with his head between his thighs, was not buried the usual Jewish way. None of these show a real burial area.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
To exclude; this leaves out
Already found, meaning a grave already known
A person who was killed
Lying down
In its normal way of burial

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think these bodies cause no טומאה. They still cause טומאה. They just do not count toward making the place a שכונת קברות.

phrases.english: GEMARA: Rav Yehuda said:
"Found" excludes one already found.
"Dead" excludes one who was killed.
"Lying" excludes one sitting.

phrases.aramaic: כְּדַרְכּוֹ — פְּרָט לְשֶׁרֹאשׁוֹ מוּנָּח בֵּין יַרְכוֹתָיו.
phrases.english: "In his manner" excludes one whose head is placed between his thighs.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה: מָצָא — פְּרָט לְמָצוּי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the exact words of the משנה's case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A known grave does not join with newly found bodies. Killed people, bodies buried sitting, and bodies bent with the head between the thighs do not count toward a burial area.

steps.title: A corpse missing a part has neither rule
steps.stepSummary: עולא בר חנינא teaches a ברייתא: a corpse that is missing a part has no תפוסה and does not count toward a שכונת קברות.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא בר חנינא taught: A corpse that is missing a part has no surrounding-earth rule and no burial-area rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with another case to add to רב יהודה's list. Here the corpse itself is missing a part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds one more exclusion. Such a corpse does not require removing the earth around it, and it does not join with others to make a burial area.

keyTerms.meaning: He taught (a ברייתא)
A corpse that is missing a part
A burial area, a cluster of graves

phrases.english: Ulla bar Ḥanina taught:
A corpse that is lacking,
has no surrounding earth
nor a graveyard.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another exclusion next to רב יהודה's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A corpse missing a part has no תפוסה and does not count toward a שכונת קברות.

steps.title: Why do all these cases not count?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind all these exclusions.
steps.simpleTranslation: And all these cases, what is the reason they do not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why all of these bodies are left out. This question sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Some exclusions have an obvious reason, like a killed person being buried where he fell. Others do not, like a body buried sitting or bent over. The גמרא wants one reason that explains them.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
These

phrases.english: And all these, what is the reason they do not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the exclusions just listed.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the bodies buried in unusual positions (sitting, or with the head between the thighs) do not count toward a burial area.

steps.title: Perhaps the dead person was a gentile
steps.stepSummary: The answer: we worry that the person may have been a גוי, since Jews are not buried this way.
steps.simpleTranslation: We say: perhaps he is a gentile.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that these unusual burials might belong to a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A Jewish burial area is shown by bodies buried the Jewish way. A body buried in a strange way may not be a Jew at all. So it cannot prove there is a Jewish burial area here.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps
A non-Jew
We say

steps.whatToRemember: Bodies buried in a non-Jewish way do not make a שכונת קברות, because we suspect they may be גוים.

phrases.english: We say perhaps he is a gentile.

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bodies may be גוים, so they do not show a Jewish burial area.

steps.title: Two bodies lying head-to-feet
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: two bodies laid so that each head is by the other's feet have no תפוסה and no שכונת קברות.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found two, with the head of this one by the feet of that one, and the head of that one by the feet of this one, they have no surrounding-earth rule and no burial-area rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא gives another case: two bodies lying in opposite directions.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Lying head-to-feet is not the normal way bodies are placed in a Jewish burial place. So these bodies do not count as normal graves and do not join to form a burial area.

keyTerms.meaning: The area by his feet
His head

phrases.english: If he found two,

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בְּצַד מַרְגְּלוֹתָיו שֶׁל זֶה,
phrases.english: the head of this one beside the feet of that one,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בְּצַד מַרְגְּלוֹתָיו שֶׁל זֶה —
phrases.english: and the head of that one beside the feet of this one —

phrases.aramaic: אֵין לָהֶן תְּפוּסָה וְלֹא שְׁכוּנַת קְבָרוֹת.
phrases.english: they have no surrounding earth nor a graveyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצָא שְׁנַיִם, רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בְּצַד מַרְגְּלוֹתָיו שֶׁל זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא of עולא בר חנינא with another excluded case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two bodies lying head-to-feet have no תפוסה and no שכונת קברות.

steps.title: Mixing known graves with newly found ones
steps.stepSummary: Three bodies made of one known and two new, or two new plus two known, do not make a burial area and have no תפוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he found three, one already known and two found for the first time, or two found for the first time and two known, they have no surrounding-earth rule and no burial-area rule.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with groups where some graves were already known and some are newly found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Known graves and newly found bodies do not join together to reach three. The next step's story spells out the rule: a burial area is made only by three known graves or by three newly found bodies, never by a mix.

keyTerms.meaning: Known, meaning a grave already known
For the first time, newly found

steps.whatToRemember: A שכונת קברות needs three bodies buried in the normal Jewish way, all of one kind: three known or three newly found. A mix of known and new graves does not combine, and unusual burials and bodies missing a part do not count toward it.

phrases.english: If he found three,
one known and two for the first time,
or two for the first time and two known —
they have no surrounding earth,
and they have no graveyard.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָצָא שְׁלֹשָׁה, הָאֶחָד יָדוּעַ וּשְׁנַיִם תְּחִילָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the ברייתא with groups that mix known and newly found graves, matching רב יהודה's exclusion of a known grave.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Known graves do not join with newly found bodies to make a שכונת קברות or bring the rule of תפוסה.

steps.title: The story of רבי ישבב and רבי עקיבא
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישבב wanted to count two known bodies plus one new body as a שכונת קברות. רבי עקיבא said a burial area needs three known or three new bodies, not a mix.
steps.simpleTranslation: There was a story with רבי ישבב. He checked and found two bodies that were already known and one that was found for the first time, and he wanted to treat them as a burial area. רבי עקיבא told him: All your work was for nothing. A burial area only applies to three known bodies or to three newly found bodies.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא tells a real story that shows the rule from step 7 in action: you cannot mix known bodies with newly found ones to make a burial area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 7 stated the rule in general terms. This story shows a great Sage who actually tried to combine them, and רבי עקיבא rejected it. The two groups are different kinds, so they do not join together to make three.

keyTerms.meaning: A story or real event, often brought to show a rule
Known bodies, graves people already knew about
Found for the first time, newly discovered
You worked for nothing, your effort was wasted

steps.whatToRemember: A שכונת קברות needs three of the same kind: three known or three new. A mix does not count.

phrases.english: There was an incident with Rabbi Yeshevav
who checked and found
two known bodies and one found for the first time,
and he wanted to make them a burial area.
Rabbi Akiva said to him:
All the effort you made, you made for nothing.
They did not say 'burial area'
except for three known bodies,
or three found for the first time.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the rule of step 7 with a story where a mix of known and new bodies was rejected.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only three known or three new bodies make a שכונת קברות; a mix does not combine.

steps.title: What is the surrounding earth?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה 'he removes them and their תפוסה' and asks what תפוסה means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: He removes them and their surrounding earth. What is this surrounding earth?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase in the משנה and asks for a definition. This sets up the next step, where an answer will be given.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that when you move a found body, you take its תפוסה with it. The word is not explained there, so the גמרא asks what it actually refers to.

keyTerms.meaning: The earth around a body that must be moved together with it
He removes them (the bodies)
What is it like? What case are we talking about?

phrases.english: He removes them and their surrounding earth.
What is meant by surrounding earth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the topic of burial areas and returns to the משנה to explain the term תפוסה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the term תפוסה in the משנה refers to.

steps.title: רב יהודה learns it from יעקב's request
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה brings the פסוק 'ונשאתני ממצרים': יעקב meant 'take some earth with me,' so the earth around a body goes with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: The פסוק says 'You shall carry me out of Egypt.' This means: take earth with me.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers the question by showing a source in the תורה for taking the earth around a body together with it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב asked יוסף to 'carry me from Egypt.' רב יהודה reads this as 'take some of Egypt with me,' meaning the earth near the body. That is the idea of תפוסה: the nearby earth is treated as part of the body when moving it.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק says, introducing a source from the תורה
You shall carry me out of Egypt
Take with me

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
The verse says
"You shall carry me out from Egypt"
phrases.notes: בראשית 47:30, where יעקב asks יוסף to bury him in ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: meaning: take some with me.
phrases.notes: He reads 'from Egypt' as 'take some of Egypt's earth along with me.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 9 by giving a פסוק as the source for תפוסה.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: תפוסה is the earth near the body, learned from יעקב's words 'carry me from Egypt,' meaning take earth with me.

steps.title: How much earth must be taken?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the exact amount of earth that counts as תפוסה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much is the measure of the surrounding earth?
steps.whatsHappening: Now that we know what תפוסה is, the גמרא asks how much of it you must take. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 10 gave the idea and the source. This question moves to the practical side: what is the amount or limit of earth that must be removed.

keyTerms.meaning: A measure, a set amount
And how much?

phrases.english: And how much is the measure of the surrounding earth?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from what תפוסה is to how much of it must be taken.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The amount of earth that makes up the תפוסה.

steps.title: Loose earth plus three fingers of solid ground
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק explains: you take the loose earth, and then dig three fingerbreadths into the untouched ground below.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק explained: You take the loose earth, and you dig three fingers deep into the untouched ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question of step 11 by quoting רבי אלעזר's measurement for תפוסה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two parts to what is taken. First all the loose, soft earth near the body. Then a further three fingerbreadths into the hard, never-dug ground under it.

keyTerms.meaning: He explained
Loose, soft earth
Untouched ground that was never dug
Fingerbreadths, a small measure of width

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar (son of Rabbi Tzadok) explained:
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets and some don't. The next step names him as the son of רבי צדוק.

phrases.english: One takes the loose earth,
and digs into the untouched ground three fingerbreadths.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 11 with a specific measurement.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Take the loose earth and dig three fingerbreadths into the untouched ground.

steps.title: A different teaching: wood chips and clumps
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges step 12 from another ברייתא where the same רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק says תפוסה means taking the wood chips and clumps of earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: They raised a challenge: And how much is the measure of the surrounding earth? רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק explained: You take the wood chips and the clumps.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second ברייתא that seems to clash with the first one. The answer to this challenge comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both ברייתות ask the very same question and quote the very same Sage. One says loose earth plus three fingers of untouched ground, the other says wood chips and clumps. So the same person seems to give two different answers.

keyTerms.meaning: They challenged, bringing a teaching that seems to disagree
Wood chips
Clumps or lumps of earth

steps.confusionAlert: This is not a new opinion from a different person. It is the same רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק, which is exactly why there is a problem.

phrases.english: They raised a challenge:
And how much is the measure of the surrounding earth?
Rabbi Elazar son of Rabbi Tzadok explained:
One takes the wood chips
and the clumps of earth.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the measurement given in step 12 using another ברייתא.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's measure of תפוסה in step 12 (loose earth plus three fingerbreadths).
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same Sage, answering the same question, is quoted in another ברייתא as saying to take wood chips and clumps, which seems to be a different description of תפוסה.

steps.title: The challenging teaching continues: sorting what was dug up
steps.stepSummary: The rest of the ברייתא from step 13: throw away what is surely not from the body, set aside what is unclear, and the rest joins together toward the amounts that spread טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He throws away what is certainly not from the body, and sets aside what is doubtful. The rest joins together toward the majority of the body's frame, toward a quarter-קב of bones, or toward a full ladle of decayed matter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא keeps quoting the ברייתא it started in step 13. This finishes the challenge against רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This version of רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's view says nothing about digging three fingerbreadths. Instead, תפוסה means sorting the loose material: clear junk is thrown out, unclear items are put aside, and whatever seems to come from the body counts toward the amounts that spread טומאה. That is a different picture from step 12, so the contradiction now stands fully.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that are certain; here, items that are surely not from the body
Doubtful items; we are not sure whether they come from the body
Joins together, combines to reach a required amount
The majority of the body's frame
A quarter-קַב of bones
A full ladle of decayed matter from a body

steps.confusionAlert: This line is not a new statement. It is the second half of the same ברייתא quoted in step 13, so it is still part of the challenge.

phrases.english: And he throws away the certain ones
phrases.notes: He means things that are certainly NOT from the body, like stones.

phrases.english: and sets aside the doubtful ones.
And the rest combines
toward the majority of the frame of a dead body,
and toward a quarter-kav of bones,
or toward a full ladle of decayed matter.
phrases.notes: These are the three amounts of a dead body's remains that make a tent טמא.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְזוֹרֵק אֶת הַוַּודָּאִין וּמַנִּיחַ אֶת הַסְּפֵיקוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא quoted in step 13
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's definition in step 12 (three fingerbreadths into untouched ground)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same תנא defines תפוסה in another ברייתא as sorting loose material, with no mention of digging into untouched ground. So he seems to contradict himself.

steps.title: His first statement was really בן עזאי's view
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's three-fingerbreadths statement was said according to בן עזאי, as a ברייתא shows.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said that according to this תנא, as a ברייתא teaches: How much is the measure of תפוסה? רבי יוחנן said in the name of בן עזאי: He takes the loose earth and digs three fingerbreadths into the untouched ground.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction. One of the two statements was רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק reporting someone else's opinion, בן עזאי's.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'three fingerbreadths' definition belongs to בן עזאי, and רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק was only repeating it. His own view is the sorting method from steps 13–14. Since the two statements are not both his personal opinion, he does not contradict himself.

keyTerms.meaning: According to this תַּנָּא (he was following someone else's view)
As it is taught in a בָּרַיְיתָא
A תַּנָּא whose opinion is the source of the three-fingerbreadth measure
Loose, crumbly earth
Untouched, never-dug ground

steps.whatToRemember: The three-fingerbreadths measure of תפוסה comes from בן עזאי. רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק was repeating it, and his own view is the sorting method.

phrases.english: He said it according to this tanna,
phrases.notes: 'It' is his first statement from step 12, the one about digging three fingerbreadths.

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
And how much is the measure of the surrounding earth?

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם בֶּן עַזַּאי:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said in the name of ben Azzai:
He takes the loose earth,
and digs three fingerbreadths into the untouched ground.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in steps 13–14
steps.terutzResolutionType: Attribution: one statement was said according to another תנא's view
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both definitions seemed to be רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק's own opinion, which would mean he contradicts himself.
steps.terutzMaskana: The three-fingerbreadths definition is בן עזאי's, and רבי אלעזר ברבי צדוק was only reporting it. His own view is the sorting method.

steps.title: Next words of the משנה: checking from that spot
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next phrase of the משנה, 'he checks from it,' to begin a new discussion.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next phrase in the משנה. It is setting up the next discussion, about checking the area around where a body was found.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The topic of תפוסה is finished, and a new section opens. The משנה said that after finding three bodies, one checks the surrounding area (up to twenty אמות) from that spot. The גמרא is about to explain this.

keyTerms.meaning: Checks, examines (the surrounding ground for more bodies)
From it, meaning from the spot where the three bodies were found

phrases.english: He checks from it.
phrases.notes: A quote from the משנה: one checks the ground for up to twenty אמות from where the body was found.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the תפוסה discussion is resolved
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One checks the area surrounding the place where three bodies were found, measuring from that spot.
